# Application Entry Point

This file serves as the main entry point for the DevTinder backend application. It initializes the Express server, sets up middleware, configures cross-origin resource sharing (CORS), connects to the database, and integrates WebSocket functionality.

## Overview

The `app.js` file is responsible for bootstrapping the entire backend application. It orchestrates the setup of core functionalities including HTTP server creation, database connection, API routing, and real-time communication via WebSockets. This file ensures that all necessary components are initialized and configured before the server starts listening for incoming requests.

## CORS Configuration

Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) is configured to allow requests from specific frontend origins.

<Info>
  This configuration ensures that only trusted frontend applications can interact with the backend API, enhancing security.
</Info>

The following origins are permitted:
*   `http://localhost:5173` (for local development)
*   `https://devtinder.yashwant.xyz` (for the deployed production environment)

## Middleware and Routing

The application utilizes several middleware functions and registers various API routes.

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="JSON Body Parsing" icon=" {} ">
    Enables the server to parse incoming JSON request bodies.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Cookie Parsing" icon=" 🍪 ">
    Allows the server to parse cookies from incoming requests.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

The following routes are mounted to handle specific API endpoints:

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Authentication" icon=" 🔑 ">
    Handles user registration, login, and token management. (`src/routes/auth.js`)
  </Card>
  <Card title="Profile Management" icon=" 👤 ">
    Manages user profile updates and retrieval. (`src/routes/profile.js`)
  </Card>
  <Card title="Connection Requests" icon=" 🤝 ">
    Handles logic for sending and accepting connection requests. (`src/routes/requests.js`)
  </Card>
  <Card title="User Management" icon=" 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 ">
    Provides endpoints for general user-related operations. (`src/routes/user.js`)
  </Card>
  <Card title="Payment Processing" icon=" 💰 ">
    Integrates with payment gateways for transactions. (`src/routes/payment.js`)
  </Card>
  <Card title="Chat Functionality" icon=" 💬 ">
    Manages real-time chat features. (`src/routes/chat.js`)
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## WebSocket Integration

Real-time communication is enabled through WebSockets. The `initializeSocket` function from `src/utils/socket.js` is used to set up the WebSocket server, which is attached to the HTTP server instance.

<Tip>
  WebSockets are crucial for features like live chat and instant notifications.
</Tip>

## Database Connection and Server Initialization

The application first establishes a connection to the database using the `connectDB` function from `src/config/database.js`. Once the database connection is successful, the HTTP server begins listening on port 5000.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Initialize Express App">
    Creates an Express application instance.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Configure CORS">
    Sets up allowed origins for cross-origin requests.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Setup Middleware">
    Initializes `express.json()` for JSON body parsing and `cookieParser()` for cookie parsing.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Register API Routes">
    Mounts all defined routers to their respective base paths.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Create HTTP Server">
    Creates an HTTP server instance using the Express app.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Initialize WebSockets">
    Integrates the WebSocket server for real-time features.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Connect to Database">
    Establishes a connection to the MongoDB database.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Start Server">
    Begins listening for incoming requests on port 5000.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Warning>
  If the database connection fails, the server will not start, and an error message will be logged.
</Warning>
